f1.quote: A direct, controlled mechanical comparison between the WTaTiVZr alloy and commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing service conditions.

f6.quote: Lattice distortions from the diverse refractory constituents lead to a more uniform stress distribution and facilitate dislocation motion.

f7.quote: The alloy’s uniform, strained lattice and improved grain boundary cohesion—attributable to the lattice distortion from multi-principal element interactions—mediate its ability to accommodate plastic deformation and resist brittle fracture.

f8.quote: Relative to pure tungsten, the WTaTiVZr alloy is expected to show higher strain-to-failure (greater plastic deformation before yielding), an improved fracture toughness (higher K_IC), and a lower creep rate under identical high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
